title: The Constitution as a Founding Inscription — preprint and comparative materials
description:
Pre-review preprint (v1.0, July 2026) and comparative datasets underlying the article The Constitution as a Founding Inscription: Social Ontology and Comparative Legal Traditions, accepted for publication in the Revista General de Derecho Público Comparado (IUSTEL), September 2026.

Datasets: ten legal traditions (Glenn's map) by point of capture, mode of inscription, technology of hardness and exemplary orders; twenty-one constitutional orders by founding act, technology of intangibility and mode of recognition of the other; the ichnological hierarchy of inscription; the twelve constitutional provisions quoted in the article; and all primary sources cited. Constitutional texts were retrieved from the Comparative Constitutions Project (Constitute).

The accepted manuscript is not included, in accordance with the journal's copyright policy.
